headline: Habiganj ASI withdrawn after video of bribery remarks goes viral
summary: The officer claimed he bought his police uniform with bribe money specifically to take more bribes, sparking widespread outrage.
details: An assistant sub-inspector (ASI) of Chunarughat Police Station in Habiganj has been withdrawn from active duty and attached to the Police Lines after a video of his bribery remarks went viral.
In the recorded video, ASI Mohammad Ilias Hossain is heard saying, "I bought this uniform with bribe money, specifically to take bribes."
The incident occurred while the officer was investigating a case filed by Noman Miah at Ranigaon Bazar in Chunarughat upazila, according to reports.
A local resident captured the incident on a mobile phone, which later circulated on social media, drawing heavy criticism of corruption within the police force.
Habiganj Superintendent of Police Md Tarek Mahmud confirmed the withdrawal and stated that an Assistant Superintendent of Police (ASP) has been tasked with investigating the incident.
Authorities are currently verifying the incident and conducting an investigation to determine if further disciplinary action is will be warranted.

headline: 1,134 deaths recorded as measles outbreak kills 6 more children
summary: The Directorate General of Health Services reports a rising death toll and over 1,200 new hospital arrivals in 24 hours.
details: According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), six more children died from measles symptoms within 24 hours, bringing the total death toll to 1,134.
The toll includes 1,032 deaths related to symptoms and 102 confirmed measles cases. The DGHS has been tracking these cases since March 15.
Dhaka Division has recorded the highest number of deaths with 468, followed by Sylhet with 179 and Rajshahi with 93.
In the last 24 hours alone, 1,291 people with symptoms arrived at hospitals nationwide, with 1,180 of them being admitted.
Across the country, 176,516 patients have been admitted so far, while 169,290 have recovered and returned home.
The total number of patients showing symptoms has reached 199,013, with measles confirmed in 21,910 of those cases.
The DGHS noted that not every patient is tested, meaning the actual number of confirmed cases may be higher than recorded.
